parameters.query: SELECT call_id FROM public.gong_calls ORDER BY call_id
SELECT id, content FROM public.gong WHERE metadata->>'call_id' = $1 AND metadata->>'doc_type' = 'transcript' ORDER BY id ASC
UPDATE public.gong SET metadata = metadata || jsonb_build_object('start_ms', $2::double precision, 'end_ms', $3::double precision) WHERE id = $1::bigint RETURNING id

parameters.content:
## Gong timestamp backfill — metadata ONLY

Backfills start_ms/end_ms on EXISTING gong rows so search_all / get_resource_context
can build from=/to= timestamped deep links (retrieval plan §7.1). Does NOT re-embed,
does NOT insert/delete any vector rows, does NOT touch the resource tree — pure
`UPDATE ... SET metadata = metadata || ...` per existing row.

Safe to re-run (idempotent, always overwrites start_ms/end_ms with a fresh computation).

Limit node defaults to 5 calls for a cheap first test — raise/remove it for the full run
(3,835+ calls on staging). Manual trigger only — never schedule this.

Matching: rebuilds the exact same flat transcript text Prepare Calls builds, finds each
existing row's stored content as a substring in it (deterministic — same input, same
text), maps the matched character range back to turn timing. Falls back to a
proportional-position estimate only if the exact match fails. Check the Summary by
Method node's counts after a run — `exact` should dominate; a high `proportional_fallback`
or `unmatched` count means something drifted (e.g. content trimmed differently) and is
worth investigating before trusting the links.
